answersReviewFindings.finding: Item 1 (tests/envoy-role-reassertion.test.ts:191 and :240): claude-envoy's typecheck is red. The base made ChannelSessionOptions.clientInstanceID required and this branch's two new startChannelSession calls predate it, outside every conflict marker of the forward merge.
answersReviewFindings.fix: Both calls pass clientInstanceID, the same literal lines 99 and 146 of that file already use.
answersReviewFindings.test: No new test: the typecheck is the check. cd packages/claude-envoy && bun run typecheck is clean where it printed TS2345 at both lines before, and bun test is 290 pass / 15 skip / 0 fail.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Item 2 (api_test.go:712): envoy-go-race is red on TestRoleHolderStateIsNamedByEachRoutesAnswer/publish. The test's own first publish keeps a copy, whose background handover resolves the holder, finds the claim lapsed and releases it before the second publish reads it, so the answer is unclaimed instead of holder_lapsed.
answersReviewFindings.fix: The test, not the code: the product behaviour is right, since any resolution may release a lapsed claim. The subtest now names its deps and holds the role's handover guard for its whole run (defer deps.delivery.roleKeepDrains.hold("reviewer")()), so no keep's handover resolves the holder while it sets its claim up. A grep for the same shape found one more rig, TestADispatchRoleRoutedEventToAnUnheldRoleReachesTheNextHolder, whose keep runs through harness.coreHandler and so carries the harness's own forward past the rig's stand-in; it now delivers through *lane.deps.delivery, so whichever handover forwards, the rig records it. Every other keep-then-claim rig keeps with keepRoleMessage, which starts no handover, or runs both handovers on one forward.
answersReviewFindings.test: The two rigs themselves, under the detector: CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=20 -timeout 3300s -run 'TestRoleHolderStateIsNamedByEachRoutesAnswer|TestAHandover|TestTheSweep|TestAKeptCopy|TestADispatchRoleRouted' ./cmd/listener -> ok 533.628s.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Item 3 (role_keep.go:476): a lane-head read that fails on the first pass ends a claim's handover at Debug, because the shared `failed` closure treats it as the keep's no-holder case. In round 4 that read sat inside the walk, after walked = true, so it was retried and reported at Error.
answersReviewFindings.fix: The lane-head read no longer goes through that closure. A read that did not answer logs its debug line, earns roleKeepDrainBackoff and the pass runs again, on the first pass as on any other; the closure, renamed holderUnresolved, is reached only by the holder resolution, where the first failure is still the keep's own case. A new headErr carries the last failing read out of the handover through ended(), so one that ends while still failing is reported by reportKeptRoleDrain at Error rather than silently.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestAHandoverRetriesALaneHeadReadThatFailedOnItsFirstPass, which fails at the previous code with 'the handover whose lane-head reads all failed reported nothing, so the lane it left undrained is said nowhere above Debug'.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Item 4 (role_keep.go:613): the lane head is read up to three times per handover, the sweep reads it before it checks the claim, and the file is 1001 lines.
answersReviewFindings.fix: walkKeptRole takes the pass's keptLaneHead and its own opening read is gone - a cursor that moved since that read fails the compare-and-swap with ErrCursorMoved and ends the walk roleKeepLaneBusy, exactly as the re-read did. The sweep reads the claim, tryHolds and starts the handover with no head read of its own, the handover's first pass ending on !head.left without resolving a holder, so a lane of an unclaimed role costs one claim read a pass and nothing else. writeRoleKeepCursor is folded into roleKeepLaneCursor.write and readRoleKeepCursor into readKeptLaneHead, with one doc reference in delivery.go following the fold. role_keep.go is 979 lines.
answersReviewFindings.test: No new test of its own: the existing walk, handover and sweep tests all drive the single read now, and TestTheSweepHandsOverALaneNoHandoverIsDraining and TestAHandoverOfAnEmptyKeptLaneResolvesNoHolder fail if the one 'anything left' test is wrong. wc -l proves the line count.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor role_keep.go:362 - the comment still names roleKeepDrainAgain, deleted in efa9c9be.
answersReviewFindings.fix: It names the switch in handOverKeptRole.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor role_keep.go:590 - 'costs no round trip' is wrong for the case the check exists for, since an unclaimed role is never in the view (kv.go:487) and the read goes to the bucket (kv.go:1145-1152).
answersReviewFindings.fix: The comment says a claimed role is in the view and costs no round trip, and an unclaimed one costs the one bucket read its miss makes.

trickyParts: This round was written twice as well: the pod was recreated again mid-round and the INFRA merge lane pushed what it found to legion/INFRA-839-rescue at cdd31a08. That branch held two files, both already identical in the rebuilt workspace, so nothing was taken back from it and the lane deleted it at my request.

The outbox package's red in this pod is a teardown permission, not a test: every test passes and the drop of storetest's isolated database is refused because legion_test is not a superuser. Whoever reads a red here should check for '--- FAIL' lines before believing the package summary.

-race -count=20 over the whole Role|Kept|Keep set does not fit a 2400 s timeout in this pod and dies with a goroutine dump that looks like a detected race until the last line is read. The five tests that can race, at the same count, finish in 533 s and are what the proof uses.
